item.title: Self-Hosted DNS Blacklist (DNSBL/RBL) Servers: rbldnsd vs postscreen vs DNSBL Management Guide
item.description:
Introduction

DNS-based Blackhole Lists (DNSBL), also known as Real-time Blackhole Lists (RBL), are one of the oldest and most effective anti-spam techniques. By querying a specialized DNS server, mail servers can instantly check whether a connecting IP address is a known source of spam, malware, or abuse — all before accepting a single byte of email data.

item.title: Self-Hosted Email Security Gateways: Proxmox Mail Gateway vs Scrollout F1 vs MailScanner
item.description:
Introduction

Email remains the number one attack vector for organizations of all sizes. Phishing, malware attachments, spam, and business email compromise (BEC) attacks all enter through the same channel: inbound SMTP. Placing an email security gateway in front of your mail server adds a critical defense layer that inspects every message before it reaches user inboxes.
